fields.name: code
fields.description: User-selected logical entry/trace key carrying the WBS identifier as text. Code presence is required by the requested join contract; the DID says codes, when used, match the approved CSDR Plan. No numeric-only, dotted-decimal or case-insensitive coding rule is invented. DI-MGMT-81334D Preparation Instructions 1.a/2.a: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5710950. FlexFile Data Group B.1 identifies the Block 11 WBS element but its native field encoding is uninspected: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5749099. MIL-STD-881F 4.3 explicitly does not make maintaining WBS numbering essential; do not require a universal numeric code scheme. https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5777624.

fields.name: level
fields.description: User-selected dictionary column retaining the electronic Index hierarchy level. Level 1 represents the total contract and successive levels are lower levels; DI-MGMT-81334D Preparation Instructions 1.b: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5710950. Routine reporting is level 3, with more detail only for the stated high-risk/high-value/high-technical-interest elements. Presence/type in the selected semantic row are user choices, not a claimed FlexFile native field. When MIL-STD-881F 2.2.3 applies, relate levels to system requirements and the product-oriented family tree; 4.2 leaves reporting levels to the contract. https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5777624.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Logical element title/nomenclature. Under the standalone DID, Index and Dictionary names match the approved contract CSDR Plan; DI-MGMT-81334D Preparation Instructions 1.c/2.b: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5710950.

fields.name: technicalContent
fields.description: Conditionally required by the standalone CWBS DID: highest-level general system description/top-level attributes, lower-level general physical characteristics, and item identity/function/physical definition. Preserve permitted generic parent definitions with detailed supporting children and the exemption from detailed descriptions of integrated GFE; no-work elements indicate not applicable. DI-MGMT-81334D Preparation Instructions 2.c: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5710950. FlexFile C.1 does not independently impose this separate technical-content field. required=false reflects cross-path conditionality, not a waiver when the standalone DID applies. MIL-STD-881F 2.2.4 also describes dictionary content including basic technical characteristics and links to detailed technical definitions, without prescribing separate machine columns. https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5777624.

fields.name: workContent
fields.description: Conditionally required under the invoked standalone CWBS or FlexFile dictionary DID; required=false avoids imposing the DID content rule on a standard-only delivery. Narrative work scope, short design/production/sustainment process, and included activity types. For standalone CWBS state reporting-contractor versus supplier/subcontractor performance; for FlexFile state supplier/subcontractor performance when present. Limit descriptions to covered contract work and, for a subcontract/supplier dictionary, exclude prime work. Mark elements with no expected work not applicable rather than dropping plan elements. Content may be one definition narrative rather than separate native columns. DI-MGMT-81334D Preparation Instructions 2.c: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5710950; DI-FNCL-82162 Preparation Instructions C.1.a/b/d: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5749099. Apply the product-oriented Program WBS and contract-only CWBS scope rules only under applicable MIL-STD-881F 2.1, 2.2.5.1 and 3.1-3.1.1. https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5777624.

fields.name: costContent
fields.description: Conditionally required under the invoked standalone CWBS or FlexFile dictionary DID; required=false avoids imposing the DID content rule on a standard-only delivery. Narrative explanation of recurring/nonrecurring effort, functional cost-element inclusion/exclusion and make/buy decisions; characterize by functional category as appropriate. No numeric cost/hour amount is required merely by this dictionary-content field. Preserve not-applicable and generic-parent qualifications. DI-MGMT-81334D Preparation Instructions 2.c: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5710950; DI-FNCL-82162 Preparation Instructions C.1.c: https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5749099.

fields.name: parentCode
fields.description: User-selected explicit hierarchy association, not a prescribed native DID column. Required for nonroot entries in the selected semantic contract; root uses null. Resolve against code and preserve the relation in the hash. Do not derive hierarchy by assuming the characters or punctuation in a code encode a level. MIL-STD-881F 2.2.3 supplies the hierarchy semantics, not this column name. https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5777624.

fields.name: requirementId

MIL-STD-881F 2.2.3 relates Program WBS levels to system requirements; it does not prescribe this identifier or a universal one-to-one trace. https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5777624.

fields.name: applicability

acceptance.rule: Apply only sources and editions invoked by the actual contract and approved CSDR Plan. For the standalone CWBS DID, inspect the solicitation-date ASSIST issues including applicable approvals, amendments, notices and revisions; use stated issues for non-ASSIST references. The current-source catalogue is not automatic evidence of contract incorporation. The DID retains a MIL-HDBK-881 reference; do not silently replace that contractual reference with MIL-STD-881F.

Under DI-MGMT-81334D, require the electronic report with both Index and Dictionary and the separate Word-compatible Dictionary file. The Index has no Excel-only mandate. The selected RTF table is only a three-entry dictionary illustration and cannot pass complete-report or plan-reconciliation checks. A standalone dictionary does not satisfy a separately invoked FlexFile delivery, and a FlexFile does not waive the separately invoked standalone deliverable.

When an approved CSDR Plan is required by the invoked standalone CWBS or FlexFile source, reject an absent or unresolved actual approved-plan reference. Under the invoked standalone DID, reconcile every approved CSDR Plan element with the Index, including not-applicable elements; reject extra Index elements. Reconcile Dictionary codes/names with Index and approved-plan codes/names. Verify the required plan approval. When an existing internal WBS is reused, retain the source-prescribed mapping to the approved plan before the conforming CWBS. No example plan content can replace the actual received plan.

Require each entry to have a nonempty code that resolves to the received WBS/Index context and a nonempty requirementId resolving to an actual requirement record. Reject either missing or unresolved join. These presence/trace rules are explicit user contract choices; the government sources do not mandate a requirementId column. The illustrative rows alone do not prove either external join.

For the selected semantic-entry contract, require unique code keys and integer hierarchy levels. Require one level-1 root with null parentCode; every nonroot parentCode must resolve without cycles and its level must be one less than the child level. Preserve all parent relationships in the baseline input. These machine-checkable transport rules are user choices, not a claimed native DID schema or mandated WBS numbering convention.

When the standalone DID reporting-depth rules apply, use routine level-3 reporting. Require deeper detail only for the lower-level elements selected under the high-risk, high-value or high-technical-interest criteria; do not expand the rule into mandatory reporting for all lower-level elements. The partial illustration is not evidence of complete reporting depth.

For the standalone CWBS technical descriptions, inspect top-level system attributes, general lower-level physical characteristics, and identification/function/physical definition of each applicable element. Permit generic parent definitions when supporting lower-level definitions provide the detail, and preserve the exception from detailed GFE-item descriptions. Do not impose this standalone-DID technical-content requirement on FlexFile C.1 alone.

For the applicable dictionary path, inspect work-content process and activity descriptions, required performing-party distinctions and contract-only scope. Supplier/subcontractor dictionaries exclude prime work. Retain no-work elements with the required not-applicable indication. Do not turn description of work into a new obligation to perform an engineering activity.

For applicable dictionary cost definitions, inspect explanations of recurring/nonrecurring effort, functional cost inclusion/exclusion and make/buy decisions, with functional-category characterization as appropriate. Preserve permitted generic-parent definitions with detailed children and not-applicable indications. Do not require actual-cost, forecast or hours amounts from these narrative clauses.
When contract GFE items are integrated, require identification as GFE under appropriate WBS elements. Do not demand detailed descriptions of those GFE items or invent additional work scope.

Under the standalone DID, prepare and deliver the first Index and Dictionary through the CSDR Submit-Review System by the required Initial Report due date; if no Initial Report is required, use the first Interim Report due date. Earlier delivery is allowed. Maintain/update the Dictionary throughout contract life; when CWBS changes, submit the updated Index and Dictionary with the next affected CSD Reports. There is no mandatory submission more frequently than CSDR submissions and no imposed sixty-day-after-award deadline. Verify the named DCARC/CSDR delivery path without inventing a successor endpoint.

For WBS dictionary data submitted under the invoked FlexFile DID, require electronic delivery in accordance with the CAPE-approved DEI/FFS unless the contract specifies an alternative format; require delivery to DCARC through CADE CSDR Submit-Review in accordance with that DID and the approved DD FORM 2794. Do not use the prior CWBS Dictionary format for a FlexFile submission. This last prohibition does not invalidate a separately invoked standalone CWBS deliverable.

For an invoked FlexFile delivery, preserve appropriate security classification in Data Group A Item 12 and proprietary/distribution statement in Item 13. Record supplied marking context at the receiver. Do not infer release authorization from an unclassified marking or create binding marking rules from inaccessible issuances.

Keep the five held issuances open where affected: DoDI 5000.88, DoDM 5010.12, DoDI 5230.24, DoDI 5200.48 and DoDM 5200.01 Vol 2. Also retain the inaccessible DoDM 5000.04 and DoDI 5000.73 and current FlexFile DEI/FFS as open gaps. Do not assert full policy, current native FlexFile encoding or FFS conformance from inspected DID text alone. A specifically supplied contractual alternative format is evaluated on its own received terms, not invented terms.

Catalogue guidance as binding=false/kind=guidance. Guidance does not independently reject this feed, does not create mandatory definition fields, and is excluded from operative baseline inputs in this and every later batch. Do not hash the governing-document or requirement-record catalogue as the feed baseline.
